title: Probabilistic Graceful Downgrade Controller for Latency-Driven Region Failover
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: during regional or tier overloads we currently trigger aggressive binary fallbacks (full region cutover or immediate model variant downgrade) which cause customer-visible latency spikes and inconsistent quality. We need a controller that uses multiple signals (429 surge, tail latency, p50/p95 increases, error-rate) to probabilistically degrade requests across region/tier/model-variant boundaries. Goals: 1) reduce blast radius by gradually shifting a fraction of traffic away from failing capacity, 2) prefer model-variant downgrades when quality impact is low, 3) provide observability and deterministic rollout so SREs/PMs can tune thresholds and recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can detect a region-level latency surge (p95 > configured threshold) and start a probabilistic rollback that shifts 5-50% traffic away from the region according to tunable decay curves

When 429 rate exceeds configured bounds for >30s, controller triggers per-tenant soft-fallback to a compatible lower-cost model variant for a sampled subset of requests and emits a decision event to tracing
Circuit breaker opens per-region/per-tier with hysteresis and exponential backoff, but does not force a full cutover unless trip persists >5 minutes
All fallback decisions are exported to tracing and a dedicated dashboard showing decision rate, observed quality delta, and user impact
Unit and integration tests cover probabilistic sampling, backoff behavior, and a simulated rollout in the staging cluster
technical_notes: Signals: use rolling windows of 10s and 5m for short/medium term detection; combine absolute thresholds and relative delta (e.g., p95 increased by >2x)
Decision function: compute a trip_score from weighted signals (latency, 429_rate, error_rate, queue_depth). Convert trip_score to probability using logistic transform to determine sampling fraction
State: controller stores per-region and per-tier decay timers and probation windows in Redis with TTLs; persistent decisions are logged to ClickHouse for audits
Fallback variants: maintain compatibility matrix in config service mapping primary model -> safe downgrade variants with expected quality penalty estimates
Safety: add per-tenant opt-out and max-fallback-per-minute guard to avoid amplifying customer impact; default global limit 20% of a tenant's traffic can be forced to downgrade in any 5m window
Latency overhead: controller decision path must add <1ms p99 CPU time; implement hot path in C++ runtime + gRPC to avoid Python overhead
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal staging rollout to canary tenants (5% traffic) with debug logging enabled; run for 48h and compare quality metrics
Phase B: narrow public canary limited to select low-risk tenants (10%) with throttled sampling and safety caps; iterate thresholds
Phase C: regional opt-in across EU and us-west, autopilot disabled (requires manual approval to escalate), observe 7 days
Phase D: enable autopilot with conservative defaults (max 10% soft-downgrade sample, 3 min probation) and a rollback toggle in Console
Rollback: immediate global kill switch via config service and automated health probe that reverts all probabilistic decisions in 30s
